items.stem: In a short-talk listening item asking for the speaker's main purpose, the best approach is to:

options.text: Listen for the overall goal, not just repeated words
options.rationale: Correct: purpose questions test gist, not word recognition.

options.text: Pick the option sharing the most words with the audio
options.rationale: Word overlap is a common distractor, not evidence of purpose.

options.text: Assume the purpose is always a complaint
options.rationale: Purpose varies; assuming one type is unreliable.

options.text: Answer before listening to save time
options.rationale: Guessing without listening is unreliable for gist items.

items.explanation: Correct: purpose questions test gist, not word recognition.

items.stem: Which TWO strategies help manage timing in the TOEIC Reading section?

options.text: Locate answers rather than reading every word
options.rationale: Correct: targeted reading saves time on detail items.

options.text: Budget time per part and move on from stuck items
options.rationale: Correct: pacing prevents running out of time.

options.text: Read each passage three times before answering
Leave all hard items for an imaginary extra section
options.rationale: There is no extra time section; this risks blanks.

options.text: Answer only the questions you find easy and skip the rest permanently
options.rationale: Unanswered items score nothing; at least an educated guess is better.
